main_body: A large brown rectangle (about 36x41 px) whose upper part is a pale olive-green block with a scalloped lower edge, resembling a hanging cloth or slab. Below it is a dark brown panel with scattered dark and magenta marks. A grey base strip sits at the bottom.
top_band: Rows 2-10/11 are pale olive (L=151), but they read as a vertical cloth or panel with a dripping, scalloped lower edge, not a horizontal top surface. It is directly followed by dark brown (L=28) at rows 11-13, then the brown body (L=65). There is no clear front-edge step between a top and a front face.
evidence: The column scan shows a 1-row outline, a 1-row brown line, a 9-10 row olive block, then dark and brown rows down to the bottom outline. The olive area fills the upper quarter of the object like a vertical face (a curtain or cloth), and the brown below is a flat front with no inset details. No top surface is drawn, and there is no front-edge line or eave shadow. The drawing is a front elevation and does not look like low furniture, so the kind does not match either.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 5 distinct colours and a median of 5 colours per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. Flat-fill coverage is 51%, against 0-13% in the references. 100% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, which gives the near-black sticker outline, while the references are tinted (1% and 33% neutral). The large olive and brown areas are flat with almost no grain, so the piece is much shallower than the Beodeul standard.
